meta.comment: Parameters of the symbol set. Stroke, tension, dots, flat apexes and keylines are computed from the design-system.json of Porto Faifo Sans, not typed by hand: change the font and the symbols follow.

grid.comment: Every recipe is drawn once on a 24-unit grid, y up, live area 2..22, in centre-line coordinates. inset is half a Regular stroke at 20 px (0.9 units): the centre line sits one inset inside the keyline, so the outer edge of a Regular stroke touches it. Heavier strokes grow both ways, as in a font (Bold = Regular + g × added stroke, g ≈ 0.5 for circles).

keylines.comment: The square keyline is narrower than the circle by the O : H ratio of Porto Faifo Sans (1320 : 1136 = 1.162), for the same reason: a circle looks smaller than two straight edges. 20 / 1.162 = 17.2 units.

14.use: Compact: lists and dense toolbars of desktop apps

16.use: Dense menus, data tables, system tray

20.use: Web default (20 px icon box), desktop

sizes.comment: text is the Porto Faifo Sans size set next to the symbol: 12px for compact labels, 13px for secondary labels, 14px for interface labels, 17px for mobile body text. All four sizes keep the true (fractional) stroke for HiDPI screens.

stroke.comment: Symbol stroke (px) = stemLower(weight) / unitsPerEm × text(size) × opticalGain. Symbols are sparser than text, so the same thickness looks lighter; 1.2 brings the 20 px Regular stroke to 1.49px, the stem of an interface label (Porto Faifo Sans Medium 14px = 1.50px). The four weights keep the stem ratios of the font: Light ×0.78, Medium ×1.20, Bold ×1.62 of Regular.

shapes.comment: dot: a true round dot 1.32 strokes wide, like the dot of i; standalone dots (more, wifi) are 1.3 times larger to stay legible. apexFlat: angles sharper than apexFlatBelow degrees end in a narrow flat cut on the grid, 1.11 strokes wide, like the apex of A and the foot of V (204 / 184). radius: centre-line radius of closed corners; the outer edge is radius + half a stroke (tension 0.59), the inner edge radius − half a stroke (0.58).

pairing.comment: Symbols set next to text centre on the math axis of Porto Faifo Sans (0.45 cap = 0.320 em), the same axis as + − × =, so a plus symbol lines up with the + character. CSS: vertical-align: calc(0.32em - <symbol size> / 2).
